items.title: Launch or rejoin Herdr
items.detail: Omarchy desktop launcher. This is the outer entry point for your session.

items.title: Move between application panes
items.detail: Move focus between AI, editor, and shell in the current Herdr tab.
items.warning: Outer terminal bindings can intercept this. Prefix → Tab cycles Herdr panes; Prefix → 1…9 selects Herdr tabs.

items.title: Cycle Herdr panes
items.detail: Next pane, or previous pane with Shift. Inherited upstream mapping.

items.title: Return to previous pane
items.detail: Toggle back to the last focused Herdr pane.

items.title: Zoom the active pane
items.detail: Give the AI transcript or editor the full tab; repeat to restore the layout.

items.title: Split a pane below
items.detail: Horizontal division creates an upper and a lower Herdr pane. This changes the current layout.
items.warning: In Omarchy, Prefix → h splits; it is not a left-navigation key.

items.title: Split a pane to the right
items.detail: Vertical division creates left and right Herdr panes. Ghostty’s Omarchy config forwards Alt+Shift+Enter.

items.title: Resize the active Herdr pane
items.detail: Direct directional resizing of the Herdr pane.

items.title: Enter pane resize mode
items.detail: Use the resize-mode help shown by the installed Herdr build for follow-on controls.

items.title: Rename the current pane
items.detail: Label the AI, editor, or shell pane.

items.title: Close the current pane
items.detail: Closes the selected Herdr pane.
items.warning: Omarchy sets confirm_close=false. Pane close can terminate the process running there; use Prefix → d to detach from the session instead.

items.title: Create a Herdr tab
items.detail: A new tab inside the current Herdr workspace.

items.title: Jump to a Herdr tab
items.detail: Select a numbered tab in the active Herdr workspace.
items.warning: Outer terminal bindings can intercept this. Prefix → Tab cycles Herdr panes; Prefix → 1…9 selects Herdr tabs.

items.title: Previous / next Herdr tab
items.detail: Move through tabs within the current workspace.
items.warning: Windows Terminal uses Alt+arrows for outer panes; use the prefix alternatives.

items.title: Reorder the current Herdr tab
items.detail: Move the tab one position backward or forward.
items.warning: Windows Terminal binds Alt+Shift+arrows to outer-pane resize. Use Herdr’s mouse menus when the chord is intercepted.

items.title: Rename the current Herdr tab
items.detail: Changes the active tab name.
items.warning: Prefix → r is rename tab in Omarchy. Resizing uses Prefix → Ctrl+arrow or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+arrow.

items.title: Close the entire Herdr tab
items.detail: Closes the tab and its panes.
items.warning: High impact: Omarchy sets confirm_close=false. Prefix → k is close tab, not “move up”.

items.title: Previous / next repo workspace
items.detail: Move between Herdr workspaces. Desktop workspaces are a separate layer.
items.warning: Windows Terminal uses Alt+arrows for its own pane focus. Prefer the prefix alternatives.

items.title: Open the workspace navigator
items.detail: Choose an existing Herdr workspace. Inherited upstream mapping.

items.title: Create an empty workspace
items.detail: For your three-pane layout, run hdw from a shell in the desired directory instead.

items.title: Rename the current workspace
items.detail: Change the Herdr workspace name.

items.title: Close the entire workspace
items.detail: Closes the workspace and its contents.
items.warning: High impact: Omarchy sets confirm_close=false. Detach with Prefix → d to leave the session running.

items.title: Detach and keep the session
items.detail: Leave the Herdr client while preserving the native session for reattachment.

items.title: Open the goto picker
items.detail: Inherited Herdr goto action; choose a destination from the running picker.

items.title: Toggle the Herdr sidebar
items.detail: Show or hide the workspace sidebar.

items.title: Enter pane copy mode
items.detail: Review and select output from the focused Herdr pane. Use this layer for an individual AI transcript.

items.title: Move within pane history
items.detail: Vim-style movement in Herdr copy mode; Ctrl+u / Ctrl+d move by half pages.

items.title: Start a copy-mode selection
items.detail: Anchor a selection, then move to extend it.

items.title: Copy the selected text
items.detail: Copy the selection from Herdr pane history.

items.title: Search pane history
items.detail: Forward search with /, backward with ?. Use n / Shift+n for next / previous match.

items.title: Leave copy mode
items.detail: Esc first clears an active selection or search; q leaves copy mode.

items.title: Show current Herdr bindings
items.detail: Runtime help is the authority for the installed, merged configuration. The help overlay supports / to filter.

items.title: Reload Herdr configuration
items.detail: Apply configuration changes in Herdr.
items.warning: Prefix → q reloads. Use Prefix → d to detach.

items.title: Open Omarchy’s Herdr help
items.detail: Desktop-level Herdr reference. Prefix → ? shows the running application’s bindings.

items.title: Toggle Neo-tree at repo root
items.detail: Both editor baselines enable the Neo-tree extra. Root means LazyVim’s detected project root.

items.title: Toggle Neo-tree at working directory
items.detail: Open the tree relative to the current working directory rather than LazyVim’s detected root.

items.title: Open Neo-tree Git status
items.detail: Shows the Neo-tree git_status source. Space → g → s is your custom Snacks Git status picker.

items.title: Open Neo-tree buffers
items.detail: Shows the Neo-tree buffers source.

items.title: Find a project file
items.detail: Fuzzy file picker at LazyVim’s detected project root.

items.title: Find files at working directory
items.detail: Use the current working directory as the picker scope.

items.title: Search text across the project
items.detail: Live grep at LazyVim’s detected project root.

items.title: Search text at working directory
items.detail: Live grep scoped to the current working directory.

items.title: Search the current word / selection
items.detail: Search the word under the cursor, or the selected text in Visual mode.

items.title: Open a recent file
items.detail: Recent-file picker.

items.title: Reopen the previous picker
items.detail: Resume the last Snacks picker.

items.title: Search and replace
items.detail: Open the Grug Far search-and-replace interface.
items.warning: Replacement operations change files; review the scope and matches before applying.

items.title: Move between editor windows
items.detail: Left, down, up, right inside Neovim, including Neo-tree and file windows. Press Esc first to ensure Normal mode.
items.warning: In Insert mode, Ctrl+k can show signature help. Use Ctrl+Alt+arrows for Herdr application panes.

items.title: Resize an editor window
items.detail: Resize the current Neovim window. This is the editor layer, within a single Herdr pane.

items.title: Choose an open buffer
items.detail: Pick an already open editor buffer.

items.title: Previous / next file buffer
items.detail: Cycle editor buffers.
items.warning: With Neo-tree focused, Shift+h is the tree’s hidden-file toggle. Use this in an editing window.

items.title: Switch to the alternate buffer
items.detail: Jump back to the previously active buffer.

items.title: Close a buffer, keep the layout
items.detail: Delete the current buffer with Snacks while preserving the editor’s window layout.

items.title: Close other buffers
items.detail: Close buffers other than the active buffer. Save changes as prompted.

items.title: Split the editor below
items.detail: Create another Neovim window below the current one.

items.title: Split the editor to the right
items.detail: Create another Neovim window to the right.

items.title: Close an editor window
items.detail: Close the Neovim window, rather than the Herdr pane.

items.title: Zoom the current editor window
items.detail: Toggle the current Neovim window’s zoom. Prefix → z zooms the whole Herdr pane.

items.title: Save the current file
items.detail: Save from an editor file buffer; also available in Insert and Visual modes.
items.warning: Focus the editing buffer first. Ctrl+S means quick jump in Neo-tree and open a split in a Snacks picker.

items.title: Format file / selected range
items.detail: Run the configured formatter on the file or Visual selection.

items.title: Rename a code symbol
items.detail: Requires an attached LSP server with rename support.

items.title: Show code actions
items.detail: Requires a provider for code actions, usually an attached LSP.

items.title: Go to definition
items.detail: Requires definition support from the attached LSP.
items.warning: Plain g → d navigates code. Space → g → d opens your contextual Git diff picker.

items.title: Find references
items.detail: Requires references support from the attached LSP.

items.title: Show symbol documentation
items.detail: Hover information from a capable attached LSP.

items.title: Previous / next diagnostic
items.detail: Navigate diagnostics in the current file.

items.title: Show diagnostics for this line
items.detail: Open the line diagnostic message.

items.title: Toggle line wrapping
items.detail: Toggle wrapping in the current editing window.

items.title: Toggle autoformat for this buffer
items.detail: Buffer-specific autoformat toggle; lowercase Space → u → f is the global toggle.

items.title: Review changed hunks
items.detail: Your custom Snacks Git diff picker, covering staged and unstaged hunks. Repository follows the current file or selected Neo-tree node; tree root is the fallback for a node without a path.
items.tags: personal personal contextual repository neotree ai review

items.title: Review grouped diff against origin
items.detail: Personal mapping passes base="origin" and group=true. Snacks compares from git merge-base with origin, grouped by file. Same contextual repository resolver as Space g d; no fetch is performed.
items.warning: The repository must resolve the ref “origin”. This is not a hard-coded origin/main comparison.

items.title: Review Git status + untracked files
items.detail: Your contextual Snacks Git status picker. Selected Neo-tree paths, real paths, and worktrees are handled; special buffers use the window working directory.

items.title: Open Lazygit at project root
items.detail: Open Lazygit using LazyVim’s root logic. Your contextual Git override applies specifically to gd, gD, and gs leader mappings.
items.warning: Git tools can stage, restore, or otherwise modify repository state. Review the selected action.

items.title: Show Git history for this file
items.detail: Use the current file’s Git history picker.
items.warning: Preview freely, but Enter checks out the selected historical version of this file into the working tree.

items.title: Search current key mappings
items.detail: Search the active Neovim keymap list. Useful for resolving version or plugin differences.

items.title: Show buffer-local mappings
items.detail: Which-key buffer-local mapping view. Inside Neo-tree, plain ? opens tree help.

items.title: Discover leader-key groups
items.detail: Press Space, then wait for which-key’s available next keys.

items.title: Quit the Neovim instance
items.detail: Quit all editor windows. Neovim’s modified-buffer checks apply.

items.title: Open a file or folder
items.detail: Open the selected node. LazyVim overrides the tree’s l mapping.

items.title: Collapse the selected folder
items.detail: Close the selected tree node.

items.title: Copy the full path for an AI prompt
items.detail: Copies the selected node’s full path as text to the system clipboard. Move to the AI pane and paste with Ctrl+Shift+V.

items.title: Toggle file preview
items.detail: Toggle the preview within the editor window using LazyVim’s use_float=false override.

items.title: Create a file
items.detail: Create an item under the selected location.

items.title: Create a directory
items.detail: Create a folder under the selected location.

items.title: Rename the selected item
items.detail: Rename the chosen filesystem item.

items.title: Copy a filesystem item
items.detail: Place the item in Neo-tree’s file clipboard; p pastes it.
items.warning: Lowercase y copies a filesystem item. Shift+y copies its path as text to the system clipboard.

items.title: Cut a filesystem item
items.detail: Prepare the selected item for a move through Neo-tree’s file clipboard.

items.title: Paste a filesystem item
items.detail: Paste a copied or cut item at the selected location.
items.warning: Pasting a cut item moves it on disk.

items.title: Delete the selected item
items.detail: Invoke Neo-tree’s deletion action for the selected item.
items.warning: Destructive filesystem action. Check the path and confirmation carefully.

items.title: Open in a vertical editor split
items.detail: Open the selected file in a side-by-side Neovim split.

items.title: Open in a horizontal editor split
items.detail: Open the selected file in a stacked Neovim split.

items.title: Toggle hidden / filtered files
items.detail: Show or hide filtered entries in the tree.

items.title: Refresh the file tree
items.detail: Refresh Neo-tree’s current source.

items.title: Fuzzy-find a tree entry
items.detail: Find filenames inside the tree. Space → / searches project file contents.

items.title: Navigate to the parent directory
items.detail: Move the tree to its parent directory.

items.title: Use the selected folder as tree root
items.detail: Set the selected directory as the tree root.

items.title: Close the Neo-tree window
items.detail: Close the explorer window and return to editing.

items.title: Show Neo-tree local help
items.detail: Display the mappings active in the focused tree.

items.title: Copy terminal selection
items.detail: Copy Ghostty’s current text selection to the system clipboard.
items.warning: Ctrl+c is normally an interrupt for the foreground terminal process, not clipboard copy.

items.title: Paste into the focused application
items.detail: Paste the system clipboard into the active AI, shell, or editor pane. Omarchy explicitly maps Shift+Insert to clipboard paste.

items.title: Copy with the Insert-key alternative
items.detail: Omarchy explicitly maps Ctrl+Insert to system clipboard copy.

items.title: Increase terminal font size
items.detail: Enlarge the text on the current Ghostty surface.

items.title: Decrease terminal font size
items.detail: Reduce the text on the current Ghostty surface.

items.title: Reset terminal font size
items.detail: Restore the configured font size.

items.title: Toggle outer window fullscreen
items.detail: Ghostty window fullscreen. Prefix → z instead zooms a Herdr pane.

items.title: Open the command palette
items.detail: Search Ghostty actions. Available in Ghostty 1.2 and later.

items.title: Open Ghostty configuration
items.detail: Open the Ghostty configuration in the configured editor.

items.title: Reload Ghostty configuration
items.detail: Apply reloadable Ghostty settings after editing its configuration.

items.title: Search Ghostty’s terminal history
items.detail: Native outer-terminal search, available in Ghostty 1.3 and later. Use Herdr copy mode to target one Herdr pane’s transcript.

items.title: Page through outer scrollback
items.detail: Scroll Ghostty’s terminal history. The focused Herdr pane maintains its own history.

items.title: Go to history beginning / end
items.detail: Jump to the top or bottom of Ghostty’s scrollback.

items.title: Previous / next shell prompt
items.detail: Ghostty 1.3.1 default. Semantic prompt navigation depends on shell integration and is most useful in a direct Ghostty shell.
items.warning: This shortcut is version-sensitive. Inspect ghostty +list-keybinds on the installed build.

items.title: Create an outer terminal window
items.detail: Create a Ghostty window, a separate desktop window from the current Herdr client.

items.title: Create an outer terminal tab
items.detail: Create a Ghostty tab. For repo organization inside Herdr, use Herdr workspaces instead.

items.title: Previous / next Ghostty tab
items.detail: Navigate Ghostty’s outer tabs rather than tabs within a Herdr workspace.

items.title: Select an outer Ghostty tab
items.detail: Select an outer tab by number when the action is performable.
items.warning: Herdr also binds Alt+digits. Use Prefix → 1…9 for Herdr tabs.

items.title: Select the last Ghostty tab
items.detail: Alt+9 selects the last outer Ghostty tab, rather than necessarily tab number nine.
items.warning: Herdr also binds Alt+9. Prefer Prefix → 9 when targeting Herdr.

items.title: Close the current Ghostty tab
items.detail: The Linux 1.3.1 default closes the whole outer tab.
items.warning: Omarchy sets confirm-close-surface=false. Use Prefix → d for a deliberate Herdr detach before closing the outer terminal.

items.title: Quit Ghostty
items.detail: Quit the terminal application.
items.warning: Broad action affecting outer terminal windows. Use Herdr’s Prefix → d when the goal is just to leave that session.

items.title: Create an outer split on the right
items.detail: Create a Ghostty split outside Herdr. Recommendation: let Herdr own your three-pane layout.

items.title: Create an outer split below
items.detail: Create a stacked Ghostty split outside Herdr.

items.title: Focus an outer terminal split
items.detail: Directional Ghostty split navigation, marked performable in the Linux defaults.
items.warning: When Ghostty can perform this action, it can consume the chord before Herdr receives it.

items.title: Zoom an outer Ghostty split
items.detail: Zoom the Ghostty split. Prefix → z is the Herdr pane zoom.

items.title: Resize an outer split by 10
items.detail: Resize the Ghostty split in the chosen direction. Super is the desktop logo key.

items.title: Resize an outer split by 100
items.detail: Omarchy adds the larger-step Ghostty split resize shortcut.

items.title: Forward a distinct Shift+Enter
items.detail: Omarchy sends CSI 13;2u to the terminal application. The focused agent decides what that event means.
items.warning: Newline and submission behavior is agent-specific. Treat the agent’s own input help as authoritative.

items.title: Open Herdr settings
items.detail: Inspect or change native Herdr settings in its own interface.

items.title: Jump to a notification target
items.detail: Focus the target associated with a notification.

items.title: Create a native Git worktree
items.detail: Herdr’s native new-worktree action. This creates Git state; it is separate from hdw and the shell ga helper.

items.title: Open pane scrollback in an editor
items.detail: Inspect the focused pane’s scrollback in an editor.

items.title: Use panes, borders and menus
items.detail: Click panes/tabs/workspaces, drag borders to resize, right-click for native menus. Pane applications can also capture the mouse.

items.title: Page through pane history
items.detail: Move by half pages or full pages in copy mode. The pane’s process keeps running.

items.title: Filter Herdr help
items.detail: Type an action or shortcut after /. Backspace edits; Ctrl+U clears the filter.

items.title: Create an AI/editor/shell workspace
items.detail: Choose exactly one selector and optionally -c. Run from an existing Herdr shell in the desired physical directory. Each invocation creates a new workspace. The editor receives ${EDITOR:-nvim} .; AI gets focus. Bare hdw prints usage.

items.title: Open or rejoin Herdr
items.detail: Run in a normal shell outside Herdr, then navigate inside the session and call hdw. To return to an already-open workspace, use the Herdr workspace navigator.

items.title: Return to Normal mode
items.detail: Leave Insert or Visual mode before using leader shortcuts.

items.title: Start writing
items.detail: i inserts before the cursor; a after it; o opens a line below. Esc returns to Normal mode.

items.title: Move through text
items.detail: Left/down/up/right; next/previous word; line start/end; file start/end. A count repeats movement, e.g. 5j.

items.title: Select text, lines or a block
items.detail: Character, line, or block selection. Windows Terminal’s Ctrl+V paste can intercept block selection; use Ctrl+Q as Neovim’s alternative when delivered.

items.title: Copy, delete, change and paste text
items.detail: yy yanks a line; dd deletes it to a register; ciw replaces the word; p pastes after the cursor. With a Visual selection, y/d/c act on that selection.

items.title: Undo or redo edits
items.detail: Undo the last edit or redo an undone change.

items.title: Repeat the last change
items.detail: Repeat the last text-changing action at a new location.

items.title: Search within this file
items.detail: Enter /text then Enter to search; n repeats in the same direction and Shift+N reverses it.

items.title: Copy selected text to system clipboard
items.detail: Select text, then type double quote, plus, y. Uses the system + register, distinct from Neo-tree’s file clipboard.

items.title: Paste the system clipboard
items.detail: Paste from the system + register. Windows integration is supplied by the configured Neovim provider.

items.title: Go back or forward after a jump
items.detail: Navigate the jump list, useful after following a definition.

items.title: Write the file
items.detail: Write the current buffer to disk.

items.title: Save and close this editor window
items.detail: Write, then close the current editor window.

items.title: Close this editor window
items.detail: Close the current Neovim window; modified-buffer checks apply.

items.title: Discard unsaved edits and close
items.detail: Force-close this editor window, discarding its unsaved changes when the buffer is abandoned.

items.title: Read the editor manual
items.detail: Use :help topic for a specific feature, e.g. :help user-manual or :help registers.

items.title: Navigate picker results
items.detail: Move down/up in results without leaving the input.

items.title: Open the selected result
items.detail: Confirm the selected result. The action depends on the picker: Git file history checks out that version.

items.title: Leave a picker
items.detail: First Escape leaves Insert mode; Escape in Normal mode closes the picker.

items.title: Inspect picker-local actions
items.detail: Show the current picker’s controls.

items.title: Toggle hidden, ignored or root scope
items.detail: Toggle hidden files, ignored files, or root/cwd scope in applicable pickers.

items.title: Open in a split, vertical split or tab
items.detail: These are picker actions, not save/paste. Outer-terminal interception still applies.

items.title: Stage or unstage a Git item
items.detail: Git diff/status picker override. Changes the index; ordinary pickers use Tab for selection.

items.title: Restore a Git item
items.detail: Git diff/status picker override requests restore/discard with confirmation. Changes file content; inspect the target.

items.title: List links in this note
items.detail: Collect links from the current note.

items.title: Find backlinks
items.detail: Find notes linking to the current note.

items.title: Browse the note’s contents
items.detail: Table-of-contents picker for headings.

items.title: Find tags
items.detail: Browse tags in the vault.

items.title: Paste an image into the vault
items.detail: Insert an image from the clipboard into 6-assets. Actual Windows image paste remains unverified; use the host note in Sources & workflow.

items.title: Create a permanent note
items.detail: New note using permanent.md in 2-permanent. Templates live in 5-templates.

items.title: Create a note from a chosen template
items.detail: Pick a template to create a note; template customizations determine its note-type folder.

items.title: Switch vault notes
items.detail: Quick-switch notes inside Neovim; this does not open the Obsidian desktop app.

items.title: Rename a vault note
items.detail: Invoke Obsidian’s rename operation. The vault’s reference-safe rename/promotion redesign remains deferred.

items.title: Search the vault
items.detail: Search note contents in the configured vault.

items.title: Insert a template into this note
items.detail: Choose a template and insert it into the current note.

items.title: Delete this vault note
items.detail: Confirms with No as default, then deletes the file directly rather than using trash. Loaded buffers are force-closed after deletion.

items.title: Pick a vault note to delete
items.detail: Choose a note, then confirm direct file deletion. This is not a trash operation.

items.title: Promote a note to another type
items.detail: Pick a destination note type, move the file, and reapply normalization. Multi-step operation, not an atomic/reference-safe guarantee.

items.title: Normalize this note’s slug
items.detail: Saves, derives a slug from the first body H1 or filename, renames if necessary, then normalizes. No confirmation; non-ASCII letters are stripped by the current slugger.

items.title: Link selected text to a new note
items.detail: Requires a single-line selection; creates a new note and replaces the text with its link.

items.title: Link selected text to an existing note
items.detail: Requires a single-line selection; pick the existing note to link.

items.title: Extract text into a new note
items.detail: Move the selected text into a new note and replace it with a link. Multiline selections are supported.

items.title: Follow a link or use the note’s smart action
items.detail: Follow a link, inspect a tag, fold a heading/frontmatter, or otherwise toggle/create a checkbox. On ordinary text it can create a task. Checkbox cycle: empty → ~ → ! → > → x → empty.

items.title: Previous or next note link
items.detail: Move between links in a vault note.

items.title: Open this note in Obsidian
items.detail: Open through the configured desktop URI handler. Requires the Obsidian app and vault registration on that host.

items.title: Toggle Markdown rendering
items.detail: Toggle rendering globally or for this buffer. The personal spec adds no shortcut. Normal-mode decorations give way to editable source in Insert/Visual mode and near the cursor.

items.title: Navigate directories and files
items.detail: Parent/down/up/enter directory. H/L go back/forward in directory history.

items.title: Open a file or choose its opener
items.detail: Enter opens; Shift+O chooses an opener. Text opens with $EDITOR in this pane, not in the existing top-right Neovim.

items.title: Select items or a range
items.detail: Space toggles and advances; v/V starts select/unselect range mode.

items.title: Copy, cut and paste files
items.detail: y copies, x cuts, p pastes. Shift+Y cancels yank. Shift+P overwrites existing destination files.

items.title: Copy a file path for the AI
items.detail: Copy the path as text; c d copies the directory, c f the filename. Clipboard delivery depends on terminal/provider support.

items.title: Create a file or directory
items.detail: Enter the name. A trailing slash creates a directory.

items.title: Rename an item
items.detail: Rename the hovered or selected item.

items.title: Move files to trash
items.detail: Trash the selected files; inspect the selected paths.

items.title: Permanently delete files
items.detail: Permanently delete the selected files, bypassing trash.

items.title: Search names or file contents
items.detail: s uses fd for filename search; Shift+S uses ripgrep for contents.

items.title: Filter or find in the current listing
items.detail: f filters the listing. / and ? find forward/backward; question mark is not Yazi help.

items.title: Jump with fzf or zoxide
items.detail: Use fzf or zoxide for navigation.

items.title: Toggle hidden files
items.detail: Both repositories show hidden files by default.

items.title: Create or switch Yazi tabs
items.detail: t then t creates a new tab. Brackets switch tabs. These are Yazi tabs inside one Herdr pane.

items.title: Inspect background file tasks
items.detail: Open the task manager to inspect file operations.

items.title: Show Yazi help
items.detail: Live local keymap help, including controls for the active component.

items.title: Return to the shell in this directory
items.detail: With the y shell wrapper, q changes the shell to the last visited directory; Shift+Q exits without changing shell cwd.

items.title: Browse files with cd-on-exit
items.detail: Open Yazi using the shell wrapper. q returns in the visited directory; Shift+Q keeps the original shell directory.

items.title: Navigate to a directory
items.detail: Existing directories use literal navigation; otherwise the zd/zoxide helper searches known locations. pwd -P shows the physical directory hdw will use.

items.title: Go up one, two or three directories
items.detail: Directory-navigation aliases.

items.title: List files or show a shallow tree
items.detail: eza aliases, directories first. The a variants include hidden files; trees are two levels deep.

items.title: Open Neovim here or on a file
items.detail: n without arguments opens nvim . directly, independent of your chosen $EDITOR.

items.title: Fuzzy-find or edit a file
items.detail: fzf with bat preview; eff opens the selected result through $EDITOR.

items.title: Search project text
items.detail: Recursive ripgrep search with line numbers. Respects ignore rules by default; rg --help explains scope switches.

items.title: Find paths by name
items.detail: Search file and directory names. fd --help lists hidden/ignored and type filters.

items.title: Read a file with highlighting
items.detail: Read with syntax highlighting and a pager. q exits the pager.

items.title: Read or query JSON
items.detail: Pretty-print JSON. Use jq filters to select or transform values; redirecting output writes a file.

items.title: Inspect Git changes
items.detail: Read worktree status and unstaged/staged diffs. The Neovim contextual pickers provide the same review loop with file navigation.

items.title: Open the Git terminal UI
items.detail: Interactive repository status, staging, commits, branches and history. Use its displayed key help; selected actions can change files and Git state.

items.title: Inspect processes or host summary
items.detail: btop opens resource monitoring; fastfetch prints a host summary. Killing a process is a separate btop action.

items.title: Create or extract a tar.gz archive
items.detail: compress creates a tar.gz; decompress extracts with tar -xzf into the current directory.

items.title: Watch and synchronize a directory
items.detail: Start rsync and keep watching. Destination-only files remain; neither implementation uses --delete. WSL tracks logs/retries/reconciliation; Omarchy’s simpler watcher has different guarantees. Remote destinations write to that host.

items.title: List or stop synchronization watches
items.detail: lsw lists; dsw stops helper-managed watches. WSL uses owned watcher records; see this host’s operations before relying on older watcher state.

items.title: Pick and send a file
items.detail: Select a file with fzf and copy it via SCP to the chosen remote destination.

items.title: Manage SSH port forwards
items.detail: Start local forwards, list them, or stop requested ports. dip uses process-pattern matching; inspect the host/ports before stopping.

items.title: Connect with reconnect support
items.detail: The wrapper retries eligible long-running interactive disconnects. Ctrl+C stops retries; explicit remote commands are not intentionally replayed.

items.title: Update mise-managed tools
items.detail: Updates mise-managed tools including AI clients. WSL retains mise’s release cooldown; Omarchy’s stock helper overrides it. System package updates are separate.

items.title: Discover any command’s complete interface
items.detail: type identifies aliases/functions/executables. Substitute a real command for command-name; --help or man supplies its full interface.

items.title: Search shell history
items.detail: fzf history picker. Inspect the selected command before executing it.

items.title: Insert selected paths
items.detail: fzf file/path picker inserts a selection at the prompt.

items.title: Pick a directory
items.detail: fzf directory picker changes the shell directory.

items.title: Complete commands and paths
items.detail: Cycle completion forwards/backwards with the configured Readline bindings.

items.title: Move to the beginning or end of input
items.detail: Readline line editing at a Bash prompt.

items.title: Erase and recover prompt text
items.detail: Kill text before/after the cursor; Ctrl+Y yanks killed text back into the input.

items.title: Interrupt the foreground command
items.detail: Send an interrupt. In Windows Terminal an active outer text selection can make this copy instead; clear the selection first.

items.title: Suspend and resume a shell job
items.detail: Ctrl+Z suspends a foreground job; type jobs to inspect jobs, then fg to resume. Detaching Herdr is usually better for leaving the whole workspace running.

items.title: Redraw the shell prompt
items.detail: Clear/redraw the display; this does not delete the shell history.

items.title: Create or remove a Git worktree
items.detail: Stock Omarchy helper: ga derives its worktree path from the current directory and calls mise trust. gd uses forced worktree removal and branch -D. Inspect the helper and preserve work before removal; WSL’s refusal guarantees do not apply.

items.title: Create or remove a Git worktree
items.detail: ga resolves the checkout root, creates a sibling linked worktree and enters it. gd confirms the actual path/branch, refuses dirty or unmerged work, and removes without force. Its HEAD must be contained in the primary checkout’s HEAD.

items.title: Copy an outer-terminal selection
items.detail: Copy selected terminal text. The tracked settings also bind Ctrl+C; with no selection it passes through to the application.

items.title: Paste into the focused pane
items.detail: Paste the system clipboard into the focused application. Tracked Ctrl+V also pastes and can intercept Neovim block selection.

items.title: Increase, decrease or reset font size
items.detail: Changes the outer terminal font size, affecting the whole displayed Herdr layout.

items.title: Search outer-terminal history
items.detail: Search Windows Terminal scrollback. Herdr copy mode targets one pane’s history.

items.title: Open the command palette
items.detail: Search available Windows Terminal actions.

items.title: Open settings or the default keymap
items.detail: Settings UI or installed defaults file. Inspect inherited keys there.

items.title: Create or switch outer-terminal tabs
items.detail: Windows Terminal tabs, separate from Herdr tabs/workspaces.

items.title: Open another terminal window
items.detail: Create a Windows Terminal window.

items.title: Duplicate an outer-terminal pane
items.detail: Tracked duplicate-pane action. This creates an outer split, not a Herdr pane.

items.title: Move between outer-terminal panes
items.detail: Defaults use Alt+arrows for directional focus and Ctrl+Alt+Left for previous pane. They overlap Herdr navigation.

items.title: Resize an outer-terminal pane
items.detail: Default resize actions overlap Herdr’s tab-reordering chords.

items.title: Scroll outer-terminal history
items.detail: Page through history or go to its beginning/end.

items.title: Toggle terminal fullscreen
items.detail: Alt+Enter is deliberately unbound in EyrWSL so Herdr receives its split-pane key.

items.title: Close the outer-terminal pane
items.detail: Closes the Windows Terminal pane. Prefix d detaches Herdr deliberately while leaving work running.

eyrarchy.name: EyrArcHy
notes: Open Herdr with herdr or Super+Ctrl+Enter. The inspected host uses Herdr 0.8.2 and Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2.
Omarchy owns the Herdr map, outer terminal and base editor. hdw invokes ${EDITOR:-nvim} .; the chosen default editor can change what appears in the top-right pane.
Stock c/cx/cy launch OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex with stock flags. hdw cc/cx/oc/ha sends full client commands. In particular, bare cx is Claude Code; hdw cx is Codex.
Ghostty can consume Ctrl+Alt+arrows and Alt+digits when an outer split/tab action is performable. Prefer Prefix Tab and prefix tab/workspace navigation.
Ghostty explicitly forwards Shift+Enter, but its meaning still depends on the AI client. Herdr consumes Alt+Enter and Alt+Shift+Enter for splits.
Omarchy’s worktree and watcher helpers are upstream-owned. Their removal/retry behavior differs from the WSL implementations; see Host helpers and Files & tools.

eyrwsl.name: EyrWSL
notes: Open herdr from a normal-user Arch shell in Windows Terminal. This guide follows the Omarchy-style Herdr map documented by EyrWSL operations, not an inspected WSL session.

Herdr configuration/keymap is retained host state, outside Stow. Check Ctrl+Space then ? on the actual host. A clean upstream Herdr instead defaults to Ctrl+B and different close/detach keys; do not assume the maps are interchangeable.
Windows Terminal defaults intercept Alt+arrows, Alt+Shift+arrows and Ctrl+Alt+Left for outer panes. Prefix Tab, prefix p/n and prefix Shift+P/N are clearer Herdr targets.
Alt+Enter passes through Windows Terminal but Herdr consumes it to split below. Tracked settings add no Shift+Enter mapping. Use the client’s own multiline/editor controls.
Ctrl+C copies when an outer selection exists; otherwise it reaches the application. Ctrl+V pastes at the terminal layer. Ctrl+Shift+C/V is the shared clipboard pair.

Neovim uses PowerShell for the + and * clipboard registers; paste removes CR characters. Autoformat starts off here. Actual Windows clipboard/image and generic Yazi opener behavior need the existing host acceptance checks.
For vault images, use the documented Windows-save-and-embed workaround. The pinned plugin has a PowerShell image path, but its actual WSL path/clipboard behavior is not established.
No stock Omarchy AI aliases or h/t/hdl launch recipes are supplied. Use herdr and full hdw commands. WSL worktree removal refuses dirty/unmerged work; watchers keep owned logs and retry/reconcile.

workflows.title: Start, continue, or return
workflows.text: In Herdr, cd to the project and run hdw with one of the four selectors. -c resumes the AI in a new layout; Prefix w returns to an existing workspace. Detach with Prefix d to leave processes running. Detach is not a guarantee of surviving a machine reboot.

workflows.title: Move a file into the AI conversation
workflows.text: Space e opens Neo-tree. Select the file and press Shift+Y to copy its path. Prefix Tab moves between application panes; paste with Ctrl+Shift+V into the AI prompt. For actual file contents, use that client’s file mention or ask it to read the path. Neo-tree y/p copies files; Yazi c c copies paths.

workflows.title: Review the agent’s changes
workflows.text: Return to Neovim. Space g d reviews hunks; Space g D compares from the merge base with origin; Space g s includes untracked files. The current file or selected Neo-tree item determines the repository. Git picker Tab stages/unstages; Ctrl+R requests restoration. Enter in file-history checkout changes the working file.

workflows.title: Read and write vault notes
workflows.text: Vault default: ~/Projects/vault, overridable with OBSIDIAN_VAULT. Space o o switches notes; Space o s searches; Space o n creates a permanent note. Editing, template, linking, promotion, deletion and rendering controls are under Vault notes. Rename/promotion/reference-safety limitations remain documented in maintenance.

workflows.title: Understand the layers
workflows.text: A keybinding is one shortcut; a keymap is the collection. The desktop routes keys to the outer terminal, then Herdr, then the focused AI/editor/shell. Herdr panes contain applications; Neovim windows contain buffers. A browser search shortcut in this guide never runs a terminal command.

workflows.title: Use the correct help
workflows.text: Prefix ? shows Herdr’s merged keys. Space s k searches Neovim mappings; ? helps in Neo-tree, but ~ or F1 helps in Yazi. AI help differs by client. Ctrl+Space is Herdr’s prefix before it can reach Neovim completion/selection; Alt+Enter splits before an AI can use it for a newline.

checks.text: Shell: version and upstream defaults. Inside Herdr, Prefix ? displays the effective map; / filters it. This guide’s map is Omarchy-style Ctrl+Space.
Run inside Neovim with the relevant file/tree loaded. Space s k searches maps; ? opens Neo-tree local help. :Lazy shows installed plugin versions.

checks.command:
yazi --version
type hdw y ga gd rsw
checks.text: Use ~ or F1 inside Yazi. type shows which shell functions/aliases actually own these names; tool --help opens a command’s full interface.
